source.title: Textual Steering Vectors Can Improve Visual Understanding in Multimodal Large Language Models
source.authors: Woody Haosheng Gan; Deqing Fu; Julian Asilis; Ollie Liu; Dani Yogatama; Vatsal Sharan; Robin Jia; Willie Neiswanger

record.tranche_reason: The study discusses shared semantics and cross-modal transfer, but its experiments test steering effects on visual-task accuracy—not similarity between representations, convergence with scale, or any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that textual steering vectors can improve visual understanding in multimodal models. These results concern transfer of steering effects, not whether representations become more similar. The paper does not measure distances or alignment between models, or test alignment as models scale or become more capable.
record.test_reason: The study extracts steering vectors from text-only LLM backbones and adds them to the hidden states of their own multimodal fine-tuned descendants (PaliGemma2, Idefics3), then reports visual-task accuracy. That is transfer within one model lineage, between a backbone and its fine-tune, not alignment between independently trained models or seeds. It reports no similarity, mapping or feature-recurrence measure, and nothing on scaling. It cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis only as background on shared semantics. The finding is a steering effect with no measure of representational alignment, so it falls outside every version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that text-derived steering vectors, especially mean shift, improve MLLM visual reasoning on CV-Bench and generalize out of distribution, while prompting barely helps. They claim this supports their hypothesis of unified cross-modal representations within these models. That hypothesis concerns a single model lineage, not convergence across models.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not apply the representation-similarity or convergence methods from the cited original sources; it extracts steering vectors from text-only backbones and intervenes on multimodal model activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Intervention method, target tokens (text, image, or both), layer and steering strength are varied or selected; the reported task accuracy depends on these intervention choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Concept steering vectors from a text-only LLM backbone (mean shift, probe, SAE) remain effective in its vision-language fine-tuned descendant. They raise spatial-relation and counting accuracy, and in a toy example shift perceived image colour, though gains vary by model and are sometimes negative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept directions in a text LLM backbone are largely preserved through multimodal post-training and act on image-token representations.

record.problems: The experiments measure task accuracy after steering rather than representational similarity or convergence. The reported OOD averages are aggregated across models and datasets; the paper does not report uncertainty for those averages.
record.rows_left_out: Individual model, intervention-method, token-type, task, and dataset results are not included because they measure steering effects on visual-task accuracy rather than any listed convergence version.

untested.parts: All: no alignment measured across independently trained models or across scale.
All: no image–caption representational alignment measured.
All: no learned maps or stitching between independent models; vectors are transferred from a backbone to its own fine-tune with no loss metric.
All: SAE features are taken from one backbone and applied to its descendant; recurrence across independent models is not tested.
All: no similarity metric is used.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not one of the original sources. Gains are not uniform: per Table 4, Idefics3 shows no significant What'sUp-A improvement under any method. Layer and strength were grid-searched on a training split, so in-distribution gains are best-of-grid values.

versions.untested_parts: Whether alignment between independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data increases with size or capability.
Whether representations of paired images and captions become more aligned as vision and language models improve.
Whether different random seeds produce shared features or subspaces.
Whether representations can be mapped between models with little loss, using linear maps, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired methods.
Whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.
Whether measured convergence depends on similarity metrics, settings, inputs, or distribution shifts.
Whether alignment is incomplete or plateaus, or is explained by shared training data or objectives.

rows.subject: PaliGemma2-3B, PaliGemma2-10B, and Idefics3-8B-Llama3 (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Added text-backbone-derived steering vectors to multimodal model activations at selected layers; the paper reports results across text, image, or both token interventions.
rows.baseline: Unsteered model performance; aggregate value not stated
rows.value: The authors state that steering interventions consistently improve spatial relationship and counting performance over baseline across the models.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across models and methods. This demonstrates transfer of steering effects, not representational alignment or convergence.
rows.check: Steering-effect accuracy, not alignment. The aggregate 'consistently improve' overstates Table 1: several cells are negative or zero (e.g. PaliGemma2-10B SAE relation -0.7, -2.0). The cited 76.0→83.3 gain is the best cell after grid search on layer and strength, so it is a selected value.

rows.subject: PaliGemma2-3B, PaliGemma2-10B, and Idefics3-8B-Llama3 (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Applied text-backbone-derived steering vectors using settings selected on CV-Bench to out-of-distribution datasets.

conditions.value: What’sUp-A, What’sUp-B, BLINK Object Localization, CLEVR, and Super-CLEVR

rows.measure: Average visual-task accuracy improvement over baseline
rows.baseline: Unsteered performance; aggregate accuracy not stated
rows.value: At least +3.9% average improvement for each of the three vector-based methods; MeanShift averaged +7.6%.
rows.note: Aggregate across models and datasets, as reported by the authors. This is out-of-distribution steering effectiveness, not a measure of representational similarity.
rows.check: Out-of-distribution steering accuracy, not alignment. Values match Table 2 averages (+6.0 SAE, +3.9 Probe, +7.6 MeanShift, +1.0 prompting). Bootstrap CIs exist in Appendix D (Tables 4–5) but cover only What'sUp-A and CLEVR, so 'uncertainty not stated' is partly wrong.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
